transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-23
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Carlos (Lucent Head of Platform), Asha (ML Eng), Tom (Infra)

Summary: initial discovery focused on p95 latency targets, concurrency requirements, streaming behavior and benchmarking approach across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments. Customer is sensitive to p95 spikes during peak payments batch processing windows and needs SOC2 + KMS compliance.

00:00 Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros - I'm Maya, AE on the account, Jordan is our Solutions Eng, and from Lucent?
00:08 Carlos (Lucent): Hey, Carlos here, Head of Platform, Asha is our ML engineer and Tom handles infra.
00:12 Jordan (Redwood): great, thanks. Today we want to understand your latency SLOs, concurrency, and whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private makes sense.
00:20 Asha (Lucent): yeah, main thing for us is p95 under load for inference for fraud scoring, so we're talking real-time-ish, like sub-200ms p95 ideally for shorter prompts, longer tails for larger context.
00:33 Tom (Lucent): to add, we process spikes during settlement windows where concurrency goes from 50 to 400 concurrent requests for short 64-token prompts. We also have some batch jobs with streaming results for longer contextual summaries.
00:46 Maya: super helpful. When you say sub-200ms, is that token latency or end-to-end generation for a 64-token completion?
00:54 Asha: end-to-end for the whole response, so generation of N tokens and the service returning them streaming is fine, but the p95 for final token should be under 200ms in peak. We can tolerate p99 being higher but we track p95.
01:08 Jordan: okay, that's an aggressive target. For context, our Hosted API with high-tier instance types historically hits around 120-220ms p95 on 64-token prompts for optimized models with streaming enabled, depends on model and batching. Dedicated with reserved GPU pools usually gives more consistent p95s under concurrency because you avoid noisy neighbors.
01:26 Carlos: what's the typical concurrency you bench with? We want to mimic our 400 concurrency spikes.
01:31 Jordan: our internal benchmarks run token/sec and latency both with fixed concurrency sweeps. Common configs: 1, 8, 64, 256 concurrency. For streaming, we measure tokens/sec and end-to-end p95. We can run an 8 and 128 concurrency test to start — but we should do 400 to mirror you.
01:46 Tom: also we have KV cache use cases — many requests share prefixes from user history — so KV cache hits matter; what's Redwood's behavior there?
01:54 Jordan: we support KV/prefix caching on the runtime. If you have high cache hit rates, effective tokens/sec improves and p95 drops significantly. We can toggle caching on in benchmarks. Note: cache warms take a bit of traffic and behavior differs between models.
02:10 Asha: model choice is important — are you validating with Llama variants or other open models? We might want FP16 or quantized runs.
02:17 Jordan: we test Llama-2, Mistral, and some mixed open models. Quantized runs (8-bit) are supported and reduce memory and cost; performance tradeoffs: quant can change latency a bit, sometimes small regressive effects, but often acceptable. We'll include quantized and full-fp tests.
02:32 Maya: quick qualification — what's your timeline and success criteria?
02:36 Carlos: timeline is 6-8 weeks to pilot, then decision end of Q2. Success criteria: p95 < 200ms for 64-token under 400 concurrency spikes, streaming with token/sec >= 4000 sustained during peak, SOC2 and KMS integration, ability to burst into Dedicated if Hosted can't meet SLOs.
02:54 Jordan: got it. On the SOC2/KMS front, our Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and is typical for regulated flows. Dedicated also supports encryption at rest and audit logs; Hosted can support SOC2 compliant handling with contract/legal controls — we'll share our compliance pack.
03:10 Tom: network topology - can Hosted guarantee region availability? We need EU data residency for a chunk of traffic.
03:16 Maya: yes, we have regional endpoints; we can route EU traffic via our EU region or do Private VPC in your region for full residency.
03:24 Asha: for benchmarks, can you run streaming with function/tool calling disabled and with top-k/top-p tuned? We have some deterministic scoring so we want consistent sampling settings.
03:32 Jordan: yes, we'll run both deterministic (greedy) and sampling configs. We'll log full seeds and outputs for you.
03:40 Carlos: cost — what's the cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated for this scale? If we need reserved capacity for 400 conc, that's significant.
03:47 Maya: high-level - Hosted is usage-based, good for ramp; Dedicated is committed monthly/annual capacity with better unit economics at scale and predictable throughput. We'll include ballpark numbers in the pricing sheet and an ROI calc for reserved vs pay-as-you-go.
03:59 Jordan: technically also autoscaling behavior matters — if you have big spikes we can configure burst policies to bump into reserved capacity or fallback to a cheaper model variant. That helps with cost vs SLO tradeoffs.
04:14 Asha: about streaming: we care about early tokens being available quickly — what's your initial token latency at p95 with streaming?
04:21 Jordan: initial token latency often benefits from prefix caching and warm KV; for cold starts it's larger. In Dedicated you can pin model instances which reduces cold-start tail. We measure initial token p95 separately — we'll capture that in the benchmark.
04:35 Carlos: logs and tracing — we need per-request traces, and per-token cost breakdowns for finance.
04:41 Maya: Redwood Console includes token-level cost/latency breakdowns and tracing hooks — we'll give you demo access.
04:48 Tom: security question — SSO, RBAC, audit trail into our SIEM?
04:52 Jordan: SAML SSO, granular RBAC, audit logs with syslog/forwarding integrations; Private gives you direct control over log retention.
05:03 Asha: ok, for the benchmark, here's our proposed test matrix: 64-token short prompt, 256-token mid, streaming 512-token long summary; concurrency sweep at 1, 8, 64, 400; deterministic vs sampling; quantized vs FP16 vs FP32. Can you run that?
05:20 Jordan: yes we can. We'll prioritize 64-token at 400 concurrency and streaming 512 at 64-128 concurrency. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
05:30 Carlos: what about model fallback and graceful degradation if a model can't meet p95s? We need consistent availability.
05:35 Jordan: our routing supports fallbacks to lighter model variants or different region/ Dedicated pool. Policies can be per-route with canary rules. We can failover to a cheaper model variant but tag responses so you can track quality drift.
05:47 Maya: any blockers on your side for a pilot?
05:50 Carlos: we'll need a security review and NDA, and we need pricing to be preliminarily approved. Also, we'd like to run a POC with your Dedicated reserved pool if costs align.
05:59 Maya: understood. We'll send the pricing and security packet after this call. Jordan will get started on the benchmarks once you share prompts and credentials for the test harness.
06:08 Asha: small nit — our infra uses strict egress policies; if you need to run private deploy we might prefer VPC peering or on-prem.
06:17 Jordan: VPC peering and private control plane options exist; note on-prem has longer lead time. We'll document network requirements.
06:24 Carlos: ok, timeline recap — send pricing/security by EOD Friday, benchmarks run next week, follow-up demo the week after with Private checklist. Decision by end of Q2.
06:34 Maya: confirmed. We'll include expected bench artifacts: p95 snapshots, raw logs, model configs, quantization settings.

[Transcript continues with technical deep dive between Jordan and Tom about kernel selection, batching and tokenization, occasional interruptions and filler words - excerpted below]
10:05 Jordan: ...the runtime chooses kernels based on seq length distribution; if your 64-token traffic dominates we pick kernels optimized for short sequences, reduces latency. Batching window tuned per SLO; higher batching reduces cost but increases latency tail.
10:30 Tom: are there metrics for batch size distribution per vertex? We want to map our traffic patterns.
10:36 Jordan: yes, we can export batch histograms and effective tokens/sec, also cache hit rates. We'll include sample dashboards.
12:12 Asha: during spikes will Dedicated guarantee CPU/GPU isolation? We've seen noisy neighbor spikes on other clouds.
12:18 Jordan: Dedicated pools are isolated and you get reserved GPUs; autoscaler doesn't evict your capacity. For hosted, we have multi-tenant nodes so there is some variability.
14:00 Carlos: want to talk about streaming token/sec target — we said 4000 tokens/sec sustained during peak. Is that feasible?
14:07 Jordan: depends on model and instance type. For an optimized quantized model on Dedicated we can often hit multiple thousands tokens/sec across the pool. We'll include tokens/sec numbers per instance type in the benchmark report.
16:40 Tom: do you support function/tool calling during streaming? Our scoring pipeline sometimes calls internal services mid-generation.
16:47 Jordan: we support tool calls but tool call latency will add to end-to-end. We can instrument and isolate the tool call step. For strict p95 you'll want to prefetch or offload heavy tool ops.
19:50 Asha: perf counters please — latency deciles, token/sec, cache hit ratio, GPU utilization split.
19:56 Jordan: ack, will include.
22:30 Maya: quick recap before we wrap. Action items and next steps?
22:36 Carlos: provide prompt set, target p95s and peak windows.
22:40 Maya: we'll send pricing and security by Friday. Jordan will run bench with 8, 64, 400 concurrency and share results in raw and dashboard form.
22:49 Jordan: adding logs and model configs to the shared S3 bucket.
22:52 Tom: Evan from infra will be on the follow-up to review VPC.
22:55 Maya: perfect. Any final questions?
23:00 Asha: none from me.
23:02 Carlos: good — thanks everyone.
23:05 Maya: thanks, we'll follow up.

Notes on transcript quality: some names and acronyms may be mis-transcribed (e.g., KV cache sometimes transcribed as "K V cash") and punctuation is imperfect.
